# Intake Brief — Herdr stage vocabulary out of sync with wl CLI (WL-0MU624MF7004WYMI)

## Problem Statement

The Herdr plugin still enumerates two stage values that the `wl` CLI no longer
accepts (`in_progress`, `completed`) and omits nothing for `done` any more, but
its display and filter paths were only partially brought in line. The result
is a stage filter that can select stages with no (`in_progress`/`completed`)
backing data and shows misleading empty worklists, and code paths that key off
`stage === 'in_progress'` semantics that no longer exist in the CLI vocabulary.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users (developers / agents)** browsing with the `f i/f n/f p/f r`
  stage-filter chords or `/wl <stage>`, who currently hit dead filter states.
- **Producers / reviewers** relying on the Herdr list to reflect the same
  pipeline stages as `wl` and the Pi TUI, so an item's stage means the same
  thing everywhere.
- **Maintainers** of the shared icon/colour maps, who need the stage vocabulary
  to be a single source of truth.

### Example User Stories

- As a **Herdr user**, I want the stage filter to cycle only through stages the
  CLI actually recognises (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`,
  `in_review`, `done`), so I never land on a filter that can only ever be empty.
- As a **Herdr user**, I want legacy items carrying `stage=done` (2,355 in the
  current DB) to render the completed-style checkmark rather than a fallback
  question mark.
- As a **Herdr user**, I want an item being actively worked (its `status` is
  `in-progress`) to keep the metadata Last-command panel even though its
  `stage` is `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.
- As a **maintainer**, I want the Herdr stage vocabulary to be derived from (or
  asserted equal to) the shared `wl` stage rules, so it cannot drift again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `STAGES` equals exactly the CLI vocabulary `['idea','intake_complete','plan_complete','in_review','done']` (`in_progress` and `completed` removed); `Stage` (and any derived types) continue to typecheck, and no Herdr code hard-codes the removed values as valid stages.
- [ ] `STAGE_MAP` accepts only the CLI-valid canonical names and supported shorthand aliases; the `progress → in_progress` alias is removed, while `intake`/`plan`/`review`/`done` aliases still resolve. `/wl progress` and `/wl completed` fail soft (no crash, no invalid filter applied) consistent with the existing `/wl <bogus>` behaviour.
- [ ] `StageFilter` cycles only the five valid stages (then clears to `null`); `fetchItemsByStage` guards unknown/invalid stages fail-soft so it never issues `wl list --stage <invalid>` and never throws (returns an empty or fallback list). A regression test proves `in_progress`/`completed`/ `bogus` cannot produce a CLI invocation and do not throw.
- [ ] Herdr behaviour that previously keyed off `stage === 'in_progress'` (the list-row stage tag suppression, the metadata-panel Last-command reservation and lookup) is re-based on `status === 'in-progress'`, so actively-worked items keep the same UI behaviour under the current status-only claim model.
- [ ] The shared icon/colour maps (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts` `STAGE_ICONS`/`STAGE_FALLBACK`/`stageColor`) include `done` mapped to the completed-style checkmark/colour, and every valid stage plus an unknown stage render deterministically (unknown falls back to the question-mark icon without throwing). New/updated tests cover `done` and an unknown stage.
- [ ] Tests are added/updated for: the exact `STAGES` list, `StageFilter` cycling/wrapping, `STAGE_MAP` alias resolution and invalid-alias fail-soft, `fetchItemsByStage` invalid-stage guarding, and status-based in-progress UI behaviour; all existing tests continue to pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and any relevant `CLI.md` / docs entries describing the Herdr stage vocabulary and filter chords. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship release pipeline.)
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Align to the CLI, do not change it.** The `wl` stage vocabulary is
  `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`, `done`
  (`.worklog/config.defaults.yaml:21-31`). Do not add stages to `wl` config as
  part of this work item.
- **Preserve legacy rendering.** 2,355 persisted items carry `stage=done`; the
  plugin must keep rendering them correctly. `done` must remain a displayable
  stage even though it is the post-release terminal stage.
- **Support legacy `stage=in_progress` rows fail-soft.** The current DB has one
  `stage=in_progress` item; removing the value from `STAGES` must not crash any
  code path that renders it.
- **Status semantics unchanged.** `status=in-progress` remains the "actively
  worked" signal (SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9); do not reintroduce a stage for it.
- **No scope creep into `wl` core** (config/validation/doctor) — those were
  handled by WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX; this item is the Herdr/shared-display
  follow-up only.
- Respect `.gitignore` / agent-framework ignore rules in searches.

## Existing State

- **CLI valid stages** (`npx tsx`/config inspection of
  `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml:21-31`):
  `idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done`. `in_progress` and
  `completed` are not accepted by `wl update`/`wl next` validation
  (`src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts:76`).
- **Herdr `STAGES`** (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:166-174`):
  `idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_progress, in_review, completed,
  done` — two invalid values present (added as legacy alias handling in
  WL-0MU3U1AMP0044WUX).
- **Herdr `STAGE_MAP`** (`worklist.ts:180-194`) includes `progress →
  in_progress` and self-mappings for `in_progress`/`done`.
- **`STAGE_STATUS`** (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:632-636`) only special-cases
  `in_review`, `plan_complete`, `intake_complete`; anything else defaults to
  `--status open`, so `fetchItemsByStage('in_progress'|'completed')` issues
  `wl list --status open --stage in_progress|completed --root-only` and returns
  an empty, misleading list.
- **`stage === 'in_progress'` keyed behaviour** remains in
  `worklist.ts:1355` (row stage-tag suppression), `worklist.ts:2020-2026`
  (metadata Last-command reservation), and `worklist.ts:6252` (last-command
  lookup). These predate the stage removal and now never fire for
  status-only claims.
- **Shared icons** (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts:51-68, 608-617`) already
  include `done` keys (added by WL-0MU3U1AMP0044WUX) but still carry
  `in_progress`/`completed` stage entries.
- **DB stage distribution** (measured `wl list --json`): `done` 2,355,
  `in_review` 6, `intake_complete` 14, `idea` 45, `plan_complete` 2,
  `in_progress` 1 (status `blocked`), `completed` 0.
- **Research note:** the seed's claim that `wl list --stage <invalid>` raises a
  CLI error was **not reproducible** in the current build — `wl list --stage
  bogus`/`--stage completed` return `success:true, count:0`. The defect is
  therefore a misleading empty filter plus a missing fail-soft guard, not a
  hard CLI error. (The validation error is real for `wl update`.)

## Desired Change

- Replace Herdr's `STAGES` with the exact CLI vocabulary
  `['idea','intake_complete','plan_complete','in_review','done']` and update
  the `Stage` type/consumers accordingly.
- Trim `STAGE_MAP` to CLI-valid names plus shorthand aliases; drop the
  `progress`/`in_progress` alias (and any `completed` mapping).
- Make `fetchItemsByStage` fail-soft for unknown/invalid stages: do not invoke
  `wl` with an invalid `--stage`, return an empty (or sensible fallback) list,
  and never throw.
- Re-base `stage === 'in_progress'` UI behaviour on `status === 'in-progress'`.
- Confirm/retain `done` in `STAGE_ICONS`/`STAGE_FALLBACK`/`stageColor` and add
  regression coverage for `done` and unknown stages.
- Prefer deriving `STAGES` from the shared status-stage rules (or assert
  equality against them in a test) so future drift is caught.
- Update `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/stage-status.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts`, and
  any other test asserting the old seven-stage list.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `STAGES` (line ~166) and `STAGE_MAP`
  (line ~180) trimmed to the CLI vocabulary; `StageFilter`; `stage ===
  'in_progress'` branches at lines ~1355, ~2020, ~6252 re-based on status;
  `/wl <stage>` help/list options at ~2522, ~3275, ~3453.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `STAGE_STATUS` (line ~632) and
  `fetchItemsByStage` (line ~658) fail-soft guard for invalid stages.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — verify/retain `done` entries in
  `STAGE_ICONS`/`STAGE_FALLBACK`/`stageColor`; ensure unknown-stage fallback
  is deterministic.
- `packages/herdr/src/stage-status.test.ts` — extend coverage for invalid
  stages and the removed `completed`/`in_progress` cases.
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — update the `STAGES` equality assertion
  (line ~289), `StageFilter` cycling/set tests, `in_progress` fixture
  semantics.
- `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts` — update `fetchItemsByStage('in_progress')`
  and `'completed'` expectations (lines ~269, ~280-286).
- `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts` — stage-list fixtures (lines ~74, ~186) and
  `done`/unknown-stage icon coverage.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `CLI.md` if it documents the Herdr stage
  vocabulary/filter chords) — document the aligned vocabulary.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX — Remove the in_progress stage** (completed): removed
  `in_progress` from `wl` config/validation; this item is the Herdr/shared
  follow-up that the stage removal implied.
- **WL-0MU3U1AMP0044WUX — Herdr extension selection list: icons sometimes render
  as error (?)** (completed): added the `done` legacy alias to `STAGES`,
  `STAGE_MAP` and the shared icon maps; this item finishes the vocabulary
  alignment for the remaining invalid values.
- **Potentially related docs:** `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`
  (`stages` list), `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts`,
  `src/status-stage-rules.ts`, `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`.
- **Potentially related work items:** `WL-0MQJGBSUS0057EI4` — Add
  ready_to_merge stage support to workflow config (completed; stage-vocabulary
  precedent); `WL-0MQRC8FFC007NNTD` / `WL-0MQRC8BE90048RHA` — status-only claim
  pattern; `WL-0MSAR110S002V26K` — Herdr grouping rules involving in_progress.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk — hidden `stage === 'in_progress'` coupling:** additional branches may
  key off the removed stage beyond those listed; mitigation: repo-wide grep for
  `in_progress`/`completed` stage usage and cover with tests.
- **Risk — display regression for legacy `in_progress` items:** the single
  persisted `stage=in_progress` item must render fail-soft; mitigation: explicit
  unknown/legacy-stage test asserting the fallback icon, no throw.
- **Risk — test fixtures encode the old vocabulary:** many Herdr tests use
  `stage: 'in_progress'` as a convenient fixture; mitigation: migrate fixtures
  to valid stages/status so tests reflect the real domain.
- **Risk — `/wl progress` user muscle-memory:** removing the alias makes it fail
  soft; mitigation: document the change in `packages/herdr/README.md`.
- **Risk — scope creep into `wl` core:** temptation to re-add an
  `in_progress`-equivalent stage or refactor the whole stage model; mitigation:
  out of scope — record as a new work item if proposed.
- **Assumption:** status-only in-progress (`status === 'in-progress'`) is the
  correct replacement signal for the removed `in_progress` stage in UI
  (confirmed by WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX).
- **Assumption:** Herdr may import from `packages/shared` (already does for
  icons), so deriving `STAGES` from shared rules is feasible; if it proves
  awkward, a test asserting equality against the shared rules is an acceptable
  fallback.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the interview ask the producer to confirm the target stage
  vocabulary?" — Answer: Not asked. The seed context plus repo inspection
  establishes the CLI vocabulary unambiguously as
  `idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done`
  (`.worklog/config.defaults.yaml:21-31`), so no producer input is required.
  Source: `wl` config inspection; WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX intake brief.
- Q: "Should `in_progress`/`completed` be kept as legacy display-only aliases
  like `done`?" — Answer: Not asked; the work-item seed explicitly asks to
  "align STAGES with the CLI vocabulary" and the shared icon maps already cover
  legacy rendering via fallbacks. Assumption: remove both from `STAGES`/
  `STAGE_MAP`; keep fail-soft rendering for legacy data. Source:
  WL-0MU624MF7004WYMI description; `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`.
- Q: "Does the reported CLI error on invalid `--stage` still reproduce?" —
  Answer (research): No. `wl list --stage bogus` and `--stage completed` both
  return `success:true, count:0` in the current build; the real defect is a
  misleading empty filter plus the missing fail-soft guard. Source: direct
  `wl list` runs against the repo DB.
- Q: "Is the in-progress UI behaviour (Last command panel, stage-tag
  suppression) still needed?" — Answer (research): Yes, but it must key off
  `status === 'in-progress'` rather than the removed `stage === 'in_progress'`
  per WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX's status-only claim model. Source:
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:1355,2020-2026,6252`.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQJGBSUS0057EI4** – Add ready_to_merge stage support to workflow config (completed)
- **WL-0MN77789Q1LZ93N4** – Failing test: in-progress boost / reSort - ancestor boost when in-progress child is completed (tests/database.test.ts) (completed)
- **WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA** – Wire read commands through cache; spawn instrumentation (completed)

# Measure the post-change benefit of mode-aware AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM

## Problem statement

WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME makes the downtime dispatcher pass a mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` to dispatched audit panes: `2` in cheap mode when a second local slot is genuinely free and the dispatch is single-flight, `1` otherwise. The wiring is live in the running `dev` build (herdr `dist/` rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38; running checkout HEAD `e1bea036` includes `6188a90d`) — **no `dev`→`main` release is required** for it to take effect on this machine.

The benefit has not been observed yet. The first post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained no dispatched audits, so the audit-only `PARALLELISM=2` path was never exercised.

This item is the operational follow-up: capture a measurement that actually exercises the path.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants to confirm the change raises cheap-window local slot utilisation without increasing remote fallback.

User story:

- *As the operator, once the mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` change is live, I want to measure a dispatched audit's Phase 2 child overlap and wall-clock in a cheap window — so I can confirm the change uses the second cheap slot and shortens Phase 2 without raising remote fallback.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-change proxy usage report covering at least one 01:00-10:00 cheap window recorded, and a dispatched audit within that window shown to overlap its Phase 2 children with the parent (peak cheap-mode concurrency 2, not 1).
2. Cheap-window local utilisation compared against the immediate pre-change cheap windows and the 2026-08-22_3 reference, and reported (up, flat, or down). Utilisation is measured by **avg concurrency (while busy) = total compute ÷ busy time** and/or **slot utilisation = total compute ÷ (window × slots)**, not by busy % (which saturates at one busy slot).
3. Remote fallback rate compared against the pre-change rate and reported (must not increase).
4. Dispatched-audit Phase 2 wall-clock (per audit, or median across audits) compared against a pre-change sequential (`PARALLELISM=1`) audit and reported.
5. If the benefit is not observed (utilisation flat/down, or fallback up), a follow-up work item is created with the finding and a proposed remedy.

## Constraints

- **Operational measurement task** — the deliverable is measurement evidence, not a code change.
- **Requires runtime data.** Proxy logs/reports live on the proxy host `192.168.0.199` (`/var/log/llama-proxy`, `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable by SSH.
- **Mechanism must be exercised.** `PARALLELISM=2` is audit-only; the measurement is void unless at least one dispatched audit runs during a 01:00-10:00 cheap window with `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2`.
- **Do not disturb existing outputs.** Run the proxy usage report with an isolated `--output-dir` so the daily cron reports are left intact.
- **Do not over-claim.** Window-level utilisation is confounded by workload volume; the change-specific claim needs the per-audit A/B.
- **Blocked on child WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA**, which captures a cheap-mode dispatched audit.

## Existing state

- The mode-aware spawn path is live in the running `dev` build: `packages/herdr/dist/downtime-worker.js` (rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38) contains the `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` wiring, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6188a90d HEAD` is true for the running checkout (`e1bea036`).
- WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME (mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`) and WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (bound the audit fan-out) are completed; no release is pending for this behaviour on this machine.
- The first post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained **no dispatched audits** — its utilisation changes (avg concurrency 1.72 vs 1.46, fallback 41.7% vs 52.8%) are therefore not attributable to this change.
- The prior measurement-plan session corrected the metric (busy % is a guardrail only) and tiered the baselines (per-audit A/B primary; pre-change windows secondary; `2026-08-22_3` reference only).

## Desired change

- Capture at least one dispatched audit in a 01:00-10:00 cheap window and confirm `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` on the audit pane.
- Produce a proxy usage report for that window (isolated output dir) and show the audit's Phase 2 children overlapping the parent.
- Compare cheap-window utilisation (avg concurrency while busy and/or slot utilisation) against the immediate pre-change cheap windows and the `2026-08-22_3` reference.
- Compare remote fallback rate (must not increase) and per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock against a pre-change sequential (`PARALLELISM=1`) audit.
- If the benefit is not observed, create a follow-up work item carrying the finding and a proposed remedy.

## Measurement method and baselines

- **Metric.** Busy % (union of ≥1-active-slot intervals ÷ duration) is a coverage/guardrail metric only — it cannot distinguish one busy slot from two. Primary metric: **avg concurrency while busy** and **slot utilisation**; plus per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap. Both are emitted by the proxy usage report's "Local model utilization" section.
- **Primary baseline — per-audit A/B (best).** The change is audit-only, so the clean comparison is a cheap-mode dispatched audit at `PARALLELISM=2` vs one at `PARALLELISM=1` (matched item, or alternating), comparing Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap per audit.
- **Secondary baseline — immediate pre-change cheap windows** (2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24, 01:00-10:00) for the util/fallback guardrails, normalised for audit and request volume.
- **Reference only — 2026-08-22_3** (`~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-22_3/`): 04:00-05:00 38.2%, 05:00-06:00 24.8% busy (the source of the cited "25-38%"); cheap avg concurrency 1.55, peak 4. Same-day runs varied widely (`2026-08-22` 49.9%/55.4%; `_2` 38.2%/55.4%), so a single window is a weak baseline.
- **Data source.** Proxy logs/reports live on the proxy host `192.168.0.199` (`/var/log/llama-proxy`, `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable by SSH from the ContextHub machine. Run the report with an isolated `--output-dir` to avoid disturbing the daily cron outputs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — mode-aware `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions()` (the `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` selection: cheap mode + genuinely free second slot + single-flight).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — spawn-option tests covering the mode-aware matrix.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` / `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the bounded audit fan-out documentation.
- `$(skill_path audit)/scripts/audit_runner.py` — honours `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` / `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` as the Phase 2 child-concurrency bound.
- Proxy host `192.168.0.199`: `/var/log/llama-proxy` (raw logs) and `~/proxy-usage-reports` (reports, including `2026-08-22_3/`).
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` and `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` — dispatch evidence (which audit was dispatched, per-mode spawn env).

## Related work

- **WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME** — Dispatched audits: use both cheap slots during Phase 2 deep analysis (mode-aware PARALLELISM) (completed) — the change under measurement.
- **WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS** — Bound dispatched audit fan-out: set AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1 in downtime pane env (completed) — the predecessor bound.
- **WL-0MTSAB7YY003R3X6** — Cheap-mode utilization follow-up: collect baselines and re-measure (completed) — the utilisation baseline methodology.
- **WL-0MUWH45RF004URWP** — Document the fast/cheap proxy slot-count contract for client logic (open).
- **WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2** / **WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q** / **WL-0MT3D584X000UD9K** — spare-capacity dispatch and per-tier free-slot minimums (completed) — the slot-gating context.
- **Child WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA** — Capture a cheap-mode dispatched audit to measure Phase 2 PARALLELISM benefit (blocker).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** no dispatched audit lands in a cheap window (observed 2026-09-25), so the mechanism is never exercised and the benefit remains unmeasured. **Mitigation:** child WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA captures one — prefer audit-tier dispatch in cheap windows, trigger one manual cheap-window audit, or extend the observation period.
- **Risk:** window-level metrics are confounded by differing request/audit volume. **Mitigation:** the primary comparison is a per-audit A/B (`PARALLELISM=2` vs `=1`), matched or alternating; window metrics are secondary and normalised.
- **Risk:** busy % saturates at a single busy slot and cannot show the second slot in use. **Mitigation:** use avg concurrency while busy / slot utilisation plus per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock; treat busy % and fallback as guardrails only.
- **Assumption:** the running build already contains the wiring (`6188a90d` is an ancestor of HEAD); no release is required.
- **Assumption:** proxy logs/reports for the relevant windows are still retained on `192.168.0.199`.
- **Scope control:** do not change the dispatch policy or the parallelism defaults here; those are separate work items (e.g. WL-0MUWH45RF004URWP). Record any such opportunity as a linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Notes

discovered-from:WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME

- Run at least one dispatched audit in a cheap window: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6188a90d HEAD` confirms the code is present; confirm `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` on the audit pane via `/proc/<pid>/environ`.
- Cheap window per the slot schedule is 01:00-10:00.
- This item is operational and assigned to the Operator; it does not block the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME code change. It is blocked on child WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA, which captures a cheap-mode dispatched audit.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was completed without additional questions — the work item description (already revised by the earlier measurement-plan session, 2026-09-25) provided sufficient context to draft a clear brief. The remaining open dependency is operational, not a requirements gap, and is captured by child **WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA** (capture a cheap-mode dispatched audit).

# Capture a cheap-mode dispatched audit to measure Phase 2 PARALLELISM benefit

discovered-from:WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5

## Finding

The mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` code is live in the running `dev` build
(herdr `dist/` rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38 and contains the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME wiring;
the running checkout HEAD `e1bea036` includes `6188a90d`). A `dev`→`main` release is
**not** required for the change to take effect.

The first full post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained **no
dispatched audits** — the downtime dispatcher selected only implement/plan/intake/
scheduled items (last audit dispatch was 2026-09-24T23:54Z in fast mode; no
`audit-*` pi sessions started in the window). Because the `PARALLELISM=2` path is
audit-only, it was never exercised, so the Phase 2 benefit is unmeasured.

Window-level metrics (proxy host 192.168.0.199): remote fallback 41.7% post vs 52.8%
pre; cheap busy 67.7% both; **avg concurrency while busy 1.72 post vs 1.46 pre**;
total compute 9h 39m post vs 7h 43m pre (both confounded by differing workload).

## Goal

As the operator, I want at least one dispatched audit to run during a cheap window so I
can measure whether mode-aware `PARALLELISM=2` makes its Phase 2 children overlap the
parent and shortens Phase 2 wall-clock, without raising remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At least one dispatched audit runs in a 01:00-10:00 cheap window, and
   `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` is confirmed on the audit pane (e.g. via
   `/proc/<pid>/environ`).
2. **Primary (per-audit A/B):** the cheap-mode `PARALLELISM=2` audit's Phase 2 wall-clock
   and child overlap (peak concurrency 2 during Phase 2) are compared against a
   `PARALLELISM=1` audit — matched item, or alternating — and reported.
3. **Secondary (window guardrails):** cheap-window **avg concurrency (while busy)** and
   **slot utilisation (total compute ÷ window × slots)** are compared against the
   immediate pre-change cheap windows (2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24, 01:00-10:00),
   normalised for audit/request volume, and reported.
4. Remote fallback rate does not increase vs the pre-change comparison.
5. Findings recorded on WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5.

## Proposed remedy (pick one)

- Prefer audit-tier work items for downtime dispatch during cheap windows, so the new
  path is exercised; or
- Trigger one manual cheap-window audit and capture the spawn env plus the proxy report;
  or
- Extend the observation period until a dispatched audit lands in cheap mode.

## Notes

- **Do not use busy % as the success metric** — it saturates at one active slot and is
  blind to the second cheap slot the change is meant to use. Use avg concurrency /
  slot utilisation plus per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock. Busy % and fallback are guardrails.
- Reference-only baseline: `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-22_3/` (04:00-05:00 38.2%,
  05:00-06:00 24.8% busy; cheap avg concurrency 1.55, peak 4). Same-day variance of the
  2026-08-22 runs was large, so window metrics alone are weak evidence.
- Proxy logs/reports live on 192.168.0.199 (`/var/log/llama-proxy`,
  `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable over SSH. Use an isolated `--output-dir` when
  re-running the report.

# Enable batch delete

## Problem statement

`wl delete` accepts only a single work-item id, so removing a set of items
requires one CLI invocation (and one auto-sync) per item. Agents and humans
cleaning up many items therefore pay repeated process-start and sync costs,
making bulk deletion slow and error-prone.

## Users

- **Agents** performing periodic cleanup/pruning of stale or superseded work
  items in batches.
- **Developers/maintainers** tidying a project and wanting to remove several
  related items in one command.

Example user stories:

- As an agent, I want to run `wl delete <id1> <id2> <id3>` so that all three
  items are deleted in one process and a single sync, instead of three
  separate syncs.
- As a maintainer, I want a per-id result summary so I can see which items
  were deleted and which failed, without re-running the command per id.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl delete <id1> <id2> ...` (variadic `<id...>`) deletes every listed work
   item; when exactly one id is supplied the existing output and behaviour are
   unchanged (backward compatible).
2. Each id is processed independently: a failure for one id (not found, invalid
   id) does not abort processing of the remaining ids, and each result is
   reported per-id.
3. The command exits with a non-zero code if any id fails, and zero when all
   ids succeed.
4. Auto-sync runs **exactly once**, after all deletions in the invocation
   complete (consistent with the current single-item behaviour); `--no-sync`
   suppresses it for the whole batch.
5. `--no-recursive` and `--prefix` apply uniformly to every id in the batch;
   with the default (recursive) behaviour, descendants of each parent are
   reported per-id.
6. JSON mode returns a stable per-id `results` array (with an overall
   `success`/`deleted`/`failed` summary) while preserving the existing
   single-id fields (`deletedId`, `deletedWorkItem`, `recursive`) for
   single-id invocations.
7. An integration test file covers: multi-id success, partial failure
   (non-zero exit while other ids still deleted), a single sync for the whole
   batch, `--no-sync`, `--no-recursive`, and single-id backward compatibility.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to the soft-delete semantics: deletion still marks items as
  `deleted` (attributed with `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) via
  `db.delete(id, recursive, opts)`; hard-delete/prune remains out of scope.
- The delete command must not begin using a destructive JSONL rewrite or
  bypass existing sync/merge protections.
- Batch processing must not double-delete descendants that are also listed
  explicitly in the same invocation; such ids must be reported coherently
  (skipped / already deleted) rather than producing a hard error.
- Follow existing variadic-id conventions used by `wl update <id...>` and
  `wl close <ids...>` for argument parsing and exit-code semantics.

## Existing state

- `src/commands/delete.ts` registers `program.command('delete <id>')` (single,
  required positional) and performs: id normalisation, existence check,
  descendant collection, `db.delete(...)`, JSON/human output, then one
  best-effort auto-sync guarded by `--no-sync`.
- `wl update <id...>` and `wl close <ids...>` already implement the variadic
  pattern, including per-id `results` arrays, continue-on-error, and non-zero
  exit when any id fails (`src/commands/update.ts`, `src/commands/close.ts`).
- `DeleteOptions` in `src/cli-types.ts` already has `prefix`, `recursive`,
  `sync`.
- `db.delete` is a per-item API
  (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`: `delete(id, recursive = true, opts?)`);
  batch behaviour belongs in the CLI command layer, not the store.
- Existing test `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` asserts the
  single-id JSON shape and auto-sync behaviour, so those fields must remain
  stable.

## Desired change

- Change the command registration to a variadic positional
  (`delete <id...>`) and loop over the ids, mirroring `close`/`update`.
- Normalise and validate each id, collect per-id results, continue on
  per-id errors, and emit a batch summary in JSON mode while retaining the
  single-id JSON shape for a one-id invocation.
- Keep the single auto-sync at the end of the invocation, after all deletions.
- Update `CLI.md` (and any other user-facing delete docs) to document the
  variadic form, per-id results, and exit-code semantics.
- Add focused integration tests for the batch behaviours listed in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — **Primary change.** Switch to `delete <id...>`,
  loop over ids, build per-id results, single terminal sync, partial-failure
  exit code, backward-compatible single-id output.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — Extend `DeleteOptions` only if new batch fields are
  needed (likely unchanged; keep minimal).
- `tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts` — **New.** Integration tests for multi-id
  delete, partial failure, single sync, `--no-sync`, `--no-recursive`, and
  single-id backward compatibility.
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` — Verify/adjust only if the refactor
  changes shared code paths; single-id expectations must still pass unchanged.
- `CLI.md` — Document the variadic `delete <id...>` form, examples, per-id
  results, and exit-code semantics.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — Read-only reference; no change expected
  (batch orchestration lives in the command layer).

## Related work

- WL-0MKZ4PSF50EGLXLN — "Batch updates" (parent of the `wl update` batch work).
- WL-0MLRSG1HH19G6L4B — "Implement batch processing for 'wl update'" —
  established the variadic-id + per-id-results + continue-on-error pattern to
  mirror.
- WL-0MLRSUXHR000EW60 — "Add unit tests for wl update batch behavior" — test
  conventions for batch CLI behaviour to reuse.
- WL-0MKRPG5FR0K8SMQ8 — "Feature: worklog close (single + multi)" — the other
  existing variadic-id command whose exit-code/output shape is the model.
- WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL — "Recursive deletion of work items with children" —
  defines the recursive descendant behaviour each batch id must preserve.
- WL-0MTFNIRXU007X7U4 — "Delete-side protection: unattributed deletes never
  override live items" and WL-0MTFNIXM3000NFVC — "Attribute real deletes:
  shared delete + CLI/API wiring" — the attribution (`deletedBy`) and sync
  protections the batch path must continue to honour.
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` — existing single-delete auto-sync tests
  that must remain green (backward compatibility guard).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: breaking single-id consumers.** Agents and the TUI may parse the
  current single-id JSON (`deletedId`, `deletedWorkItem`, `recursive`).
  *Mitigation*: preserve those fields when exactly one id is supplied; add the
  batch `results` array without removing existing keys; keep the existing
  test file green.
- **Risk: duplicate/descendant ids in one batch** (e.g. deleting a parent and
  one of its children in the same call) causing confusing double-delete
  errors. *Mitigation*: deduplicate repeated ids and treat ids already removed
  as descendants earlier in the batch as skipped/already-deleted in the per-id
  result rather than hard failures (see AC2/Constraints).
- **Risk: sync runs more than once** if the loop naively reuses the current
  post-delete sync block per id. *Mitigation*: restructure so sync is invoked
  once after the loop; test with a multi-id invocation (AC4).
- **Scope-creep risk:** requests to add `--hard`, `--all`, filters, or
  interactive selection during batch delete. *Mitigation*: record extra ideas
  as linked work items; keep this item limited to variadic ids + per-id
  reporting + single sync.
- **Assumption:** `db.delete` remains unchanged and the batch logic is purely
  CLI-layer orchestration.
- **Assumption:** exit-code and per-id-result conventions should match
  `wl update`/`wl close` for consistency.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is the intended UX `wl delete <id1> <id2>` (variadic positional ids),
  consistent with `wl update <id...>` and `wl close <ids...>`, with a single
  sync at the end?"
  — Answer: **Assumption (agent, Map), not yet confirmed by producer.** The
  seed description explicitly states "allow commands such as
  `wl delete <id1> <id2>`" and "delete all the items identified before running
  the sync commands", which matches this design. Source: work-item
  description WL-0MUI83ZTX005RN93. *OPEN QUESTION for producer:* confirm the
  variadic-positional UX vs. a `--file`/stdin list input.
- Q: "How should per-id failures and exit codes behave?"
  — Answer: **Assumption (agent, Map):** continue processing remaining ids and
  exit non-zero if any id fails, matching `wl update`/`wl close`. Source:
  `src/commands/update.ts`, `src/commands/close.ts`. *OPEN QUESTION for
  producer:* confirm fail-fast is not preferred.
- Q: "Should single-id output remain backward compatible?"
  — Answer: **Assumption (agent, Map):** yes — preserve existing single-id JSON
  fields to avoid breaking `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` and existing
  consumers. Source: `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts`.
- Note: This intake was auto-dispatched on an unclaimed/idea item; the seed
  description was judged sufficient to draft the brief without an interactive
  round (per intake § Interview "Skip the interview when seed context
  suffices"). The assumptions above are recorded for producer review.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO** – Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item (completed)
- **WL-0MLUGOZO6191ZMWQ** – Improve sync test coverage (completed)
- **WL-0MMLT5UJC02BRTDB** – Finalize push rate-limit handling: create PR and tests (repro) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: abort, ac2, ac4, acceptance, accepts (+278 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: abort, accepts, add, adjust, agent (+251 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: abort, ac2, ac4, add, agent (+243 more)

# Fail closed when the proxy `/slots` detail is unavailable; remove the inaccurate count-based fallback

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher can make a dispatch decision from the llama-proxy's
`available_slots` count when per-slot `/slots` detail is absent, empty
(`slots: []`) or flagged stale (`slots_stale: true`). That count is not
trustworthy (it can overcount the budget, and `ownerLeaseCount()` can report 0
on incomplete lease data), so a dispatch can land on a slot that is not actually
free. The operator has decided the dispatcher must **fail closed** — refuse to
dispatch — whenever the per-slot detail is unusable, and the inaccurate
count-based fallback must be removed.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** running overnight downtime dispatch: wants an
  assurance that the dispatcher never dispatches onto a leased or busy slot,
  even if that means no dispatch at all while the proxy cannot serve accurate
  per-slot detail.
  - *As a producer, I want the dispatcher to refuse to dispatch when the proxy
    cannot report per-slot detail, so that I never get two agents fighting over
    one slot.*
  - *As an operator, I want a distinct, observable "fail-closed" reason in the
    decision log and herdr header, so that I can tell "no dispatch because no
    trustworthy slots" apart from "no dispatch because there is no work".*
- **Downtime dispatcher** (system actor): must derive its free-slot budget from
  a single trusted source (the per-slot array), not from an unverifiable count.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the status payload has no usable per-slot detail — `slots` absent,
   `slots: []`, or `slots_stale: true` — the dispatcher does **not** dispatch,
   and records a **distinct** fail-closed reason in the decision log
   (`.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) with a stable header token distinct
   from `slot-owner` / `contention`.
2. The count-based fallback functions (`countBasedFreeSlots`,
   `countBasedSpareCapacity`, `leaseReserve`, `ownerLeaseCount`) are **removed**
   from `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, with no remaining call sites
   (verified by `rg` and a clean TypeScript type-check).
3. `freeSlots` is **always** derived from the per-slot array
   (`countFreeUnownedSlots(usablePerSlotSlots)`); the raw `available_slots`
   count is never used as a dispatch budget, and `evaluateIdle()` / `tick()`
   cannot admit a dispatch when per-slot detail is unusable.
4. New regression tests pinned to the exact live payload from
   WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F (`total_slots: 3`, `available_slots: 1`, `slots: []`,
   `slots_stale: true`, held owner lease, live dispatched pane) assert
   `dispatched === false` and the distinct fail-closed reason; superseded
   tests that asserted the removed count-based fallback are deleted or
   rewritten.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
   (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`) to state the
   fail-closed contract.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fail closed only** — no fallback to the count, and no re-introduction of a
  cached last-good `/slots` response.
- **No proxy changes** — the llama-proxy is out of scope (tracked in
  llm-manager, e.g. LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ); only the herdr consumer changes.
- **Do not weaken other gates** — contention depth, code freeze, review-queue,
  attempt cap and the per-slot ownership rules must behave exactly as today.
- **Observability is mandatory** — a total fail-closed stop must be diagnosable
  from the decision log and header token, not silent.
- **Operational acceptance** — on a proxy that cannot serve usable `/slots`
  detail, the dispatcher will perform **no** downtime dispatch; this is the
  operator's explicit intent (recorded in the work-item create comment).

## Existing state

- `usablePerSlotSlots(status)` returns `null` for `slots` absent, `[]`, or
  `slots_stale: true`; `null` is currently treated as "use the count-based
  path".
- `tick()` computes `freeSlots = perSlotSlots ? countFreeUnownedSlots(perSlotSlots) : status.available_slots`;
  `evaluateIdle()` falls back to `countBasedSpareCapacity()` /
  `isIdleStatus(available_slots)`; `tick()` mirrors that in its `slotOwned`
  qualifier via `ownerLeaseHeld && … && !countBasedSpare`.
- Four count-based helpers exist: `countBasedFreeSlots`, `countBasedSpareCapacity`,
  `leaseReserve`, `ownerLeaseCount` (the last also feeds the `slotOwned`
  qualifier). They were introduced by WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F to avoid a stall.
- Dedicated tests for that feature live in the
  `stale/empty slots fallback + count-based spare capacity (WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F)`
  describe block in `downtime-worker.test.ts` (~line 11917).
- `active_query` is parsed and required by `parseLlamaStatus` but is not used
  for idle/busy detection (the sole signal is `local_active_query`).

## Desired change

- Turn the "unusable per-slot detail" condition into a hard fail-closed
  precondition: no usable `slots` ⇒ no dispatch + distinct decision reason.
- Delete the four count-based helpers and every call site, including the
  `countBasedFree`/`slotOwned` branches in `tick()` and the count fallbacks in
  `evaluateIdle()`.
- Make `freeSlots` uniformly `countFreeUnownedSlots(usablePerSlotSlots)`.
- Remove the now-dead `active_query` field from the parser/type where it is
  provably unused (confirm the exact boundary during planning — the parser's
  fail-closed handling of genuinely required fields must be preserved).
- Update the decision-header token map and the two documentation files to
  describe the fail-closed contract; rewrite the feature's regression tests to
  pin the new behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Remove `countBasedFreeSlots`,
  `countBasedSpareCapacity`, `leaseReserve`, `ownerLeaseCount`; convert
  `usablePerSlotSlots` into the fail-closed availability predicate; add the
  fail-closed gate + distinct reason in `tick()`/`evaluateIdle()`; derive
  `freeSlots` from `countFreeUnownedSlots` only; update `decisionHeaderToken`;
  drop the unused `active_query` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Rewrite the
  `(WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F)` describe block; add live-payload regression tests
  asserting no dispatch + the fail-closed reason; remove tests of the deleted
  helpers.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Update the stale/empty per-slot fallback
  sections (`~L669`, `~L998–L1056`) to the fail-closed contract.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update the idle/per-slot fallback description
  (`~L450–L534`, `~L869–L879`) to the fail-closed contract.

## Risks and assumptions

### Risks

- **Silent total outage (behavioural).** On a proxy that serves unusable
  `/slots` detail, downtime dispatch stops entirely. Mitigation: the distinct
  fail-closed reason and header token make this visible; the change is
  intentional and operator-approved.
- **Observability gap.** If the new reason is rate-limited (10-minute window)
  or the header token is not mapped, the stop is less visible. Mitigation: map
  the token in `decisionHeaderToken` and assert it in a test.
- **Coverage loss.** Deleting the WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F tests could remove the
  only regression guard for the original stall. Mitigation: AC4 pins the exact
  live payload as a fail-closed (no-dispatch) regression test.
- **Over-broad validation change.** Removing `active_query` from the parser
  could loosen fail-closed validation. Mitigation: confirm the exact field
  boundary during planning.
- **Scope creep.** The proxy-side cached-detail follow-up (LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ)
  must remain in llm-manager, not be pulled into this item.

### Assumptions

- The live llama-proxy is expected to serve accurate per-slot detail; failing
  closed on older/stale proxies is acceptable and is the operator's explicit
  intent.
- The exact removal scope (the candidate list) is a planning decision; planning
  may identify further legacy code shown to be inaccurate.
- The name of the new fail-closed reason/token is a planning decision.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUFP30T2003OX1F** — introduced the count-based fallback (now to be
  removed) after a `slots: []` + `slots_stale: true` stall.
- **WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28** — parent RCA on dispatcher stalls.
- **WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2** — spare-capacity dispatch feature (per-slot session).
- **WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME** — per-slot ownership gate (the other half of the
  stall fix).
- **WL-0MU8809SZ0022VZG** — count-based single-slot ownership protection.
- **WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW** — owner-lease + contention gates.
- **WL-0MU1DWXO600153OI** — precedent: removed the wrong (cumulative)
  contention signal.
- **WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3** — precedent: removed the inaccurate client-side
  running-pane cap.
- **LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ** — proxy-side cached-detail follow-up (llm-manager,
  external).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed context (the work item's create comment and description) was
sufficient to draft this brief and contained the operator's explicit decision,
so no interactive interview round was required.

- **Q: Is failing closed — no dispatch when the proxy cannot serve usable
  `/slots` detail (including on pre-feature proxies) — the intended behaviour,
  accepting that downtime dispatch stops entirely in that case?**
  — **Answer (operator, 2026-10-07):** Yes. "The operator has now decided the
  correct behaviour is to fail closed instead." Source: WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW
  create comment and item description (Goal / Background / Assumptions).
- **Q: Are proxy-side changes in scope?**
  — **Answer (operator, seed context):** No. "Changes to the llama-proxy itself
  (tracked in llm-manager)" are out of scope; the proxy-side cached-detail
  follow-up is LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ. Source: item description (Scope).
- **Q: Should a last-good `/slots` cache be re-introduced?**
  — **Answer (operator, seed context):** No. Re-introducing a cache of the last
  good `/slots` response is explicitly out of scope. Source: item description
  (Out of scope).

### Open questions

None. Remaining choices (the fail-closed reason name/token and the exact
`active_query` removal boundary) are planning-level decisions, not requirement
ambiguities.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MUV0VEFW007ZBB7** – Raise default downtime idle threshold to 75s so active sessions reclaim freed slots before dispatch (completed)
- **WL-0MS68V35Y002RZRA** – Remove legacy wlCount setting from Herdr plugin (completed)
- **WL-0MPE9J3M6009JMN6** – Update documentation for Pi-based TUI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: absent, acceptable, acceptance, active, always (+149 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mu87zgpp0029v28, 0mufp30t2003ox1f, absent, active, always (+142 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, active, always, array, available (+114 more)
